strand_b.title: Co-creating climate-resilient cities: a multi-method participatory approach for future scenario building and prioritization
strand_b.authors: Havva Ebrahimipour, Monika Mačiulienė, Anna Maria Kotrikla, Franz-Ferdinand Rothe, Gintarė Gulevičiūtė, Aelita Skaržauskienė, Kristina Kovaitė, Amalia Polydoropoulou, et al.
strand_b.summary:
Co-creating climate-resilient cities: a multi-method participatory approach for future scenario building and prioritization. Abstract While global frameworks such as the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) call for participatory planning processes that embed local priorities into future-oriented climate action, mainstream urban planning and governance approaches often remain rigid and disconnected from local concerns, leading to a critical vision-to-decision gap.
This study introduces and tests a multi-method participatory foresight framework for developing locally grounded climate-resilient urban futures, bridging the gap between community-led visioning and formal administrative prioritization.
strand_b.relevance_note: Derived EU relevance; admitted because foresight methodology is substantive and relevant to R&I/S&T or strategic-policy practice, not merely a trend/scenario output.

strand_b.title: Governance logics and foresight functions: European strategic foresight in contrastive perspective
strand_b.summary:
Governance logics and foresight functions: European strategic foresight in contrastive perspective. Rather, it contributes by specifying this context-dependence through the lens of governance logics and by showing how the same foresight methods perform different institutional functions across technocratic, market-managerial, networked and anticipatory governance settings.
The purpose of the article is to develop a governance-sensitive framework that links foresight methods to institutional functions in public decision-making.
